tweet_summary: A split-screen 'before and after' image of a man — healthy with roses on the left, emaciated and wrapped in a Ukrainian flag on the right — captioned as a real Ukrainian soldier who returned home after 730 days at war.
why_note_decision: The image is AI-generated, not a real photograph. It is a recycled, widely-debunked 'after 730 days of war' AI composite that circulates across platforms. Multiple knowledgeable repliers independently flag it as AI (one citing a detected Google SynthID watermark via reverse-image/AI-detector checks; another noting 'we debunked this last year'), and the seecheck.org analysis cited in the original note also identifies it as generated. Presenting an AI image as a real soldier's homecoming is checkable misinformation that, ironically, undermines the genuine documented suffering it imitates, so a note is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note states the image is AI-generated and not a real photograph of a Ukrainian soldier returning after 730 days. Strong notes may reference identifying evidence (Google SynthID watermark detected via AI-detector/reverse-image checks) and that the image is a recycled fake debunked previously. The note must NOT accept the image as authentic, and need not take any stance on the war itself. Cite credible AI-detection/fact-check evidence (seecheck.org, SynthID detection, or reverse-image debunk). Reject any note treating the photo as real.
reference_note: This before/after image of a Ukrainian soldier is AI-generated, not a real photograph. It is a recycled fake (a Google SynthID watermark is detected via AI-detector checks) that has circulated and been debunked previously. https://seecheck.org/index.php/2025/07/09/the-image-of-the-accelerated-aging-of-the-ukrainian-soldier-is-generated/

fact_check.claim_verdict: false - image is AI-generated, not a real photo
fact_check.notes: seecheck.org analyzed this 'accelerated aging Ukrainian soldier' image as generated (July 2025); the image recirculates regularly. Replies independently confirm AI origin, including a Google SynthID watermark detected via reverse-image/AI-detector checks, and note prior debunking. AI-generated Ukrainian-soldier media is a well-documented disinformation genre. Original CN note's verdict is correct; reference note keeps the seecheck source (the Reddit link is weaker).

importance.lens_rationale: 82k impressions; AI imagery of war suffering passed as real both spreads falsehood and corrodes credibility of genuine documentation of the war — worth correcting, moderate stakes.
